title: Monomial Occurrence in the Trail-Present Case
summary: General monomial prediction certifies absence when no trail exists but is inconclusive when a trail exists; the open task is to decide whether the target monomial appears.

formal_statement.body: For ciphers defined over fields, general monomial prediction can certify that a specific monomial $m$ is absent from the cipher's polynomial representation when no general monomial trail leads from $m$ to that representation, but it provides no information when at least one such trail exists. Develop a refinement that, in the trail-present case, determines whether $m$ actually appears, equivalently whether its corresponding coefficient $c$ is nonzero.

scope.domain: Field-based algebraic and integral cryptanalysis of cipher polynomial representations using general monomial prediction.
assumptions: The cipher is defined over a field.
parameters: m: the specific monomial whose occurrence is being tested
c: the coefficient corresponding to m in the cipher's polynomial representation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine, when at least one general monomial trail exists, whether m appears in the polynomial representation, equivalently whether c is nonzero.

citations.label: On the Field-Based Division Property: Applications to MiMC, Feistel MiMC and GMiMC

progress.summary: The source presents general monomial prediction as a one-sided test: no trail certifies absence, while the existence of a trail leaves occurrence unknown. The trail-present case remains unresolved.
